claims.claim_text: The Republican budget plan discussed in 2012 would fundamentally change Medicare.
Opposition to privatizing Medicare or converting it into a voucher program.
Opposition to requiring seniors to pay thousands of dollars more annually while the value of their Medicare benefits falls.
Medicare is a binding moral commitment to U.S. seniors.
At the time of the 2012 platform, nearly 50 million older Americans and Americans with disabilities rely on Medicare annually.
The new U.S. health care reform law discussed in 2012 strengthens Medicare through additional benefits, fraud prevention and improved patient care.
Over ten years, the new U.S. health care reform law discussed in 2012 will save the average Medicare beneficiary $4,200.
As of 2012, President Obama's crackdown on health care fraud is characterized as the most successful ever.
By the 2012 platform, President Obama's crackdown on health care fraud has recovered $10 billion from health care scams.
Commitment to build on the health care reforms described in 2012 rather than eliminate Medicare's guarantees.
As of 2012, the new U.S. health care reform law is closing the Medicare prescription-drug coverage gap known as the doughnut hole.
By the 2012 platform, more than five million seniors have saved money through closing the Medicare prescription-drug coverage gap; the average saving in the preceding year was $600.
The Medicare prescription-drug coverage gap will be permanently closed by 2020.
